factual_methodological.summary: The revision removes the only source-traceability/precision blocker. The central thesis was rechecked against EIA diesel data, RBA primary remarks, U.S. Treasury yield data and contemporaneous first-line reporting on the 28 September oil/Hormuz development; no central numeric or causal claim was changed in revision 1.

taxonomy.summary: The fixed daily Global Macro classification remains valid under political-economy-markets with controlled dimensions, geography, topics, war-armed-conflict phenomenon, brief format and daily cadence.

translation.summary: EN and PT-BR remain materially equivalent after removing the same Brazil-specific section from both locales; thesis, evidence, caveats, visuals and source traceability are aligned.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: The opening is thesis-led, headings are analytical, no QA/template language is exposed, and the previously unsupported Brazil paragraph is no longer present.

contextual_depth.summary: The report connects refining/logistics constraints to delivered fuel prices, inflation transmission and monetary-policy sensitivity without ornamental background.

visual_evidence_readiness.signature: 1 analytical Markdown table + 1 explicit diesel line chart + 1 causal flow in each locale
visual_evidence_readiness.summary: Meets the brief visual floor with source-traceable values and equivalent units/mechanisms in EN and PT-BR.

novelty_repetition.summary: Against the 25–27 September public Global Macro editions, the lead delta is refined-product/refining stress relative to the crude headline, rather than another repetition of the long-yield or sovereign-fragmentation thesis.

political_neutrality.summary: Geopolitical claims are attributed/descriptive and the report makes no electoral recommendation, ranking, endorsement or outcome prediction.

revision_delta.summary: Revision 1 only removes the Brazil-specific section identified in the rejection and adds revision metadata; the central factual thesis, numbers, charts, causal flow and conclusion were not silently altered.

contrary_evidence: The energy shock remains selective rather than a uniform global risk-off event; cross-asset behavior does not show synchronized defensive positioning.
Verified normalization of Hormuz throughput, lower freight/insurance premia, improved refinery availability and a material reversal in U.S. diesel would weaken the product-squeeze thesis.
limitations: Brent, dollar and Treasury levels are time-sensitive and may reprice after publication.
U.S. retail diesel is a direct U.S. series and should not be treated as a proxy for global refined-product prices.
The report identifies a transmission mechanism, not a claim that all economies or sectors experience the energy shock uniformly.
notes: Revision 1 resolves the sole blocker from the 2026-09-28 rejection by removing the unsupported/imprecise Brazil-specific section in both locales. Immediate public-state recheck found no canonical bundle for MT-GM-2026-09-28. Approval is bound to the exact current pending and EN/PT-BR blobs.

en.title: Global Macro — Diesel, not crude, is becoming the sharper inflation transmission channel
en.deck: Refined-product inflation is outrunning the crude headline, widening the transmission from Hormuz into freight, prices and monetary policy as Australia approaches another rate decision.
en.regime: Selective tightening with downstream energy stress: refined-product constraints are broadening inflation transmission while long yields and the dollar remain restrictive.
en.key_risk: A persistent diesel and middle-distillate squeeze could embed transport and distribution inflation even if crude prices stabilise, prolonging monetary tightening across exposed economies.
